newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Coil and ABB in maintenance deal.
newsitem.headline: Coil and ABB in maintenance deal.

text.p: Belgian aluminium coatings company Coil said on Tuesday it had signed a maintenance agreement with Belgian ABB Service, a unit of Swedish-Swiss engineering group Asea Brown Boveri.
Coil said the annual 60 million Belgian francs contract should help profitability by cutting down the time it takes to repair the company's equipment by outsourcing the work to ABB.
"A machine breakdown costs 20,000 francs an hour. That's too costly," Coil chief executive officer Charles van der Haegen told a news conference.

"It's neccessary, from today, to improve our competitiveness on the European market by working 365 days a year, seven days a week, night and day. Now, we have that extraordinary opportunity with ABB," van der Haegen added.

Coil is a European leader in the aluminium treatment market, working for a number of large European steel makers. In 1996, it made an operating profit of 70 million francs on sales of 487 million francs and opened a new 1.2 billion francs coatings line, its fourth.

Van der Haegen reiterated the company aims at an annual 25 percent increase in turnover and a 20 percent rise in its net margin. He said it also wants to be in a leading position on the American and Asian packaging markets over the next 30 years.
Van der Haegen also repeated that the company was unhappy with its listing on the Paris segment of the Euro.NM market.
"Forty percent of our total capital is in Paris. We are unhappy with the way our share performs," he said.

Van der Haegen said in a newspaper interview last month that the company was considering seeking a secondary listing for its shares on the Brussels segment of the Euro.NM market, saying French investors had shown little enthusiasm toward the company.

Euro.NM (New Market) wants to create a common technological platform for trading small company stocks on the Paris, Brussels, Amsterdam and Frankfurt bourses. The Paris NM was launched in February 1996 and the others were launched earlier this year.
